name: More chess games than atoms in the universe

hook_variants.template: The number of possible chess games is bigger than the number of atoms in the universe.
Which is bigger: chess possibilities or atoms in the universe?
There's a number so huge that even the universe can't count that high.

sections.text: Chess has around 10 to the power of 120 possible games. The observable universe has about 10 to the power of 80 atoms.
The Shannon number — named after Claude Shannon — estimates 10^120 game paths.
sections.subtitle: possible chess games

sections.text: The universe only holds 10^80 atoms. The chessboard wins by 40 zeroes.
sections.title: the race

sections.text: Every chess game ever played on Earth is a rounding error in that space.
sections.title: scale

sections.text: That's why no machine can ever 'solve' chess by brute force.
sections.title: Ways a game can go
sections.label: 10^120 branches

sections.text: Follow for more numbers that break your brain.
